column6: Two patterns held side by side; the wallet is being chosen the way a phone case is.
Four university marks in one frame; the school is the product and the wallet is the substrate.
Coastal Collection Vol. 3 numbers the drop; volume three tells her there were two she missed.
A wallet and a wristlet being clipped together; the system is what she is buying into, not the piece.
A soft-drink licence on a card holder; the brand she likes is being worn rather than drunk.
RESTOCK above a named collection; she is being told a sell-out happened and is happening again.
A collaboration held up next to the drink it references; the joke and the product are the same object.
A sealed pen turned over in a car; the packaging is doing the work of justifying the price.
Premium wallets and accessories with the ownership line underneath; who made it is part of the object.
Veteran owned and operated set as large as the product name; the provenance is the differentiator.
Two words and a machined edge in macro; a pen is being photographed like a watch.
Veteran owned in Columbus, Ohio; the town is named because specificity is what makes provenance land.
A luxury fountain pen given a sulking face; the incumbent is being mocked rather than out-specified.
This pen will outlive you, handwritten; permanence is the claim and the handwriting is the proof of use.
Still on the fence names his hesitation directly; the code and the warranty are both aimed at it.
RFID shield rendered as a badge; an invisible threat needs an icon before it can be sold against.

column2: The Woman Buying For Her Man
column6: Proving my husband wrong again; she is the buyer and the joke is that he did not ask for it.
Perishable, please keep cool printed on the box; the cold chain is the argument that this is real food.
Defense wins championships over a dog on a pitch; the discount is the actual offer underneath the gag.
The dog's name and a portion size printed on every pack; personalisation is the proof of care.
